thread:
sam: FYI discovered weird RBAC fallout after last night's IdP rollout. SCIM provisioning started returning 403s and several service account ops show KMS AccessDenied. Immediate impact: group membership changes not applied and a bunch of users flagged as inactive. Logs: 
```
2026-03-21T01:12:03Z scim-provisioner error="AccessDeniedException: kms:Decrypt denied" principal=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/scim-provisioner
2026-03-21T01:12:05Z scim-provisioner http 403 POST /Groups -> {"error":"forbidden"}
```
Anyone awake? @ops-lead @lia-security

toni: I'm up. quick check: did the IdP cert rotate + did infra-automation run a KMS key rekey or policy update? sometimes the rotation pipeline tightens policies. sam can you paste the deploy event id?

sam: deploy id infra-deploy-20260321-01. We rotated SAML cert and ran idp-healthcheck script. No deliberate KMS rekey from my notes. infra-bot shows a PutKeyPolicy event at 01:11:58 UTC by infra-automation though.

infra-bot: [AUDIT] event=PutKeyPolicy user=infra-automation resource=alias/scim-provisioner time=2026-03-21T01:11:58Z change=policy_set id=pkp-8891

lia-security: run CloudTrail filters for PutKeyPolicy and UpdateAssumeRolePolicy. Check recent IAM role policy statements for scim-provisioner and any denies on kms:Decrypt. Also check whether the key was rotated (ScheduleKeyDeletion/ReEncrypt).

toni: grabbing iam policy and key policy now. hold on.

toni: key policy snapshot: found a deny statement added covering principals outside a whitelisted list. `scim-provisioner` not in whitelist. That would explain kms:Decrypt failure. Also there's an IAM inline policy update that removed `kms:Decrypt` from the role via a restrictive condition.  Both changed at 2026-03-21T01:11:57-01:12:00Z window.

ops-lead: mitigation steps: 1) temporarily reopen key policy to include scim-provisioner so it can decrypt, 2) bump SCIM deprovision grace to 48h and pause scheduled prune, 3) disable the infra-automation job that enforces policy hardening until we audit it. sam/Toni can you apply 1 and 2 now?

sam: on it. applying key policy restore and increasing grace. Commands: 
```bash
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id alias/scim-provisioner --policy file://allow-scim-provisioner.json
kubectl patch deployment scim-provisioner -n infra -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"scim","env":[{"name":"SCIM_DEPROV_GRACE_HOURS","value":"48"}]}]}}}}'
```

lia-security: also add an audit alert for any PutKeyPolicy that removes principals used by runtime services. We need diffs shipped to security slack + PagerDuty at least for a 1h window after rotation.

toni: after applying patch I'm seeing KMS decrypt succeed again in the logs and SCIM PATCH/POSTs returning 200s. sample: 
```
2026-03-21T01:15:12Z scim-provisioner http 200 PATCH /Users/567 user=bob@example.com action=addToGroup
```

ops-lead: good. triage notes: root cause is automation that applied a lock-down key policy during IdP rollout. remediation: require code owners approval for infra-automation PRs that change KMS policies used by runtime services; add preflight validation to rotation job to ensure essential principals remain allowed; add CI test that checks key policy post-rotation.

lia-security: add runbook updates: - document fallback auth path for SCIM if key access broken - include re-encrypt helper for tokens and a one-click rollback for key policy - list owners for each key. Also treat infra-automation as high-risk in vuln triage board.

toni: one more hiccup: a handful of users were deprovisioned before we widened the grace window. we'll run a reconciliation job to re-evaluate any users whose state changed in the incident window. scheduling that now and marking with incident tag INC-2026-0320-02.

ops-lead: assign follow-ups: @toni write incident blameless postmortem draft, @lia-security add gating for PutKeyPolicy changes, @sam add CI key-policy check and ensure infra-automation requires manual approval for KMS policy changes. ETA EOD.

sre-bot: [INCIDENT] service=scim-provisioner incident=INC-2026-0320-02 status=mitigated mitigated_by=toni mitigated_at=2026-03-21T01:20:45Z

sam: closing note: re-encryption was not required because policy rollback restored access to the existing key. if we had rotated keys we'd need to re-encrypt stored tokens and rotate secrets in Vault. I'll add a short checklist to the runbook.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from ops-lead, :warning: from lia-security)
